subject: maths
title: Primary 3 Perpendicular and Parallel Lines
seo_title: P3 Perpendicular and Parallel Lines Worksheets: Free Primary 3 Maths with Answers (MOE Syllabus)
standard_text: Perpendicular and parallel lines; drawing them on a square grid
meta_desc: Free P3 maths practice: find perpendicular and parallel lines in shapes, letters and real life, and draw them on a square grid. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Perpendicular lines meet at a right angle; parallel lines stay the same distance apart and never meet.
key_sub: On a grid: PQ goes 2 right and 1 up, a parallel line goes 2 right and 1 up, a perpendicular line goes 1 right and 2 down.
body_html:
Perpendicular lines

Perpendicular lines meet at a right angle. A small square in the corner shows the right angle. The lines can cross, meet at one end, or not touch at all: if we make them longer, they meet at a right angle.

We can write AB ⊥ CD for “AB is perpendicular to CD”.

Parallel lines

Parallel lines stay the same distance apart. They never meet, however long we make them. They can go across, up and down or slanting, and they can be different lengths. Matching arrow signs show parallel lines.

We can write AB // CD for “AB is parallel to CD”.

On a square grid

Count the squares from one end of the line to the other. A parallel line has the same steps. A perpendicular line swaps the two numbers and turns the slant.

Example

Line PQ goes 3 squares right and 1 square up. How does a line perpendicular to PQ go?

Swap the numbers: 1 and 3. Turn the slant: up becomes down.

Answer: 1 square right and 3 squares down

Example

Line AB goes 2 squares right and 1 square up. Line CD goes 4 squares right and 2 squares up. Are they parallel?

For every 2 squares right, both lines go 1 square up. They have the same slant.

Answer: Yes, AB // CD

In shapes and around us

A rectangle has 2 pairs of parallel sides and 4 right angles. A trapezium has exactly 1 pair of parallel sides. Railway tracks, ladder rungs and zebra crossings show parallel lines. The bars of a window cross at right angles.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Thinking perpendicular lines must touchMake the lines longer: do they meet at a right angle?
Thinking slanting lines cannot be parallelCheck the gap: does it stay the same all the way?
Thinking parallel lines must be the same lengthLength does not matter, only the direction
Calling any crossing lines perpendicularCheck the corner with a right angle
On a grid, using the mirror slant for a perpendicular lineSwap the steps and turn: 2 right 1 up becomes 1 right 2 down

faq.q: What do P3 students learn about perpendicular and parallel lines?
faq.a: They find perpendicular lines (lines that meet at a right angle) and parallel lines (lines that stay the same distance apart), and draw both kinds of lines on a square grid.

faq.q: How do I explain parallel lines to my child?
faq.a: Show railway tracks or the lines of a running lane: the gap between the two lines stays the same, so they never meet. On grid paper, a parallel line goes the same number of squares across and up.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake with perpendicular lines?
faq.a: Thinking that the lines must touch. Two lines are perpendicular if they would meet at a right angle when we make them longer.

faq.q: Is this topic in the MOE syllabus for Primary 3?
faq.a: Yes. Identifying perpendicular and parallel lines and drawing them on a square grid are part of Geometry in the MOE 2021 Primary 3 syllabus. Angles in degrees follow in P4.

items.q: A horizontal line and a vertical line meet. How are the two lines?
items.e: A horizontal line and a vertical line always meet at a right angle, so they are perpendicular.

items.q: Are lines AB and CD perpendicular?
c: No, they do not meet at a right angle
Yes, they would meet at a right angle
items.e: Both lines go straight across and stay 3 squares apart. They are parallel, so they never meet.

items.q: Which pair of lines is perpendicular?
items.e: Picture A shows a line that meets the other line at a right angle. It is turned, but the angle is still a right angle.

items.q: Are lines AB and CD perpendicular?
c: No, they do not meet at a right angle
Yes, they meet at a right angle
items.e: CD goes straight up from AB. It meets AB at a right angle, so the lines are perpendicular. They do not need to cross.

items.q: Which capital letter has perpendicular lines?
items.e: The 2 lines of L meet at a right angle. The lines in V, X and N meet at a slant.

items.q: Priya says AB and CD are not perpendicular because they do not touch. Is she right?
c: No, if we make CD longer, it meets AB at a right angle
items.e: Make CD longer upwards and it meets AB at a right angle. Lines can be perpendicular even when they do not touch.

items.q: Line CD is vertical. Line AB is perpendicular to CD. What kind of line is AB?
items.e: A line perpendicular to a vertical line goes straight across, so AB is horizontal.

items.q: Two lines meet at a right angle. What are they called?
items.e: Lines that meet at a right angle are perpendicular lines. Parallel lines never meet.

items.q: Are lines AB and CD perpendicular?
c: No, they do not meet at a right angle
Yes, they meet at a right angle
items.e: CD goes 4 squares right and 6 squares down. It crosses AB at a slant, not at a right angle. Crossing lines are not always perpendicular.

items.q: Are lines AB and CD perpendicular?
c: No, they do not meet at a right angle
Yes, they meet at a right angle
items.e: AB goes 2 squares right and 1 square up. CD goes 1 square right and 2 squares down. The steps swap and turn, so the lines meet at a right angle.

items.q: Nurul says that any two lines that cross are perpendicular. Is she right?
c: No, they must cross at a right angle
Yes, crossing lines are always perpendicular
Yes, if the lines are long
items.e: Perpendicular lines meet at a right angle. Lines can cross at a slant, and then they are not perpendicular.

items.q: Which pair of lines is NOT perpendicular?
items.e: Picture D shows a line that meets the other line at a slant, not at a right angle. The other three pairs are at right angles.

items.q: Are lines AB and CD perpendicular?
c: No, they do not meet at a right angle
Yes, they meet at a right angle
items.e: CD meets AB, but it slants: it goes 2 squares right and 4 squares up. A line perpendicular to AB would go straight up.

items.q: Are lines AB and CD perpendicular?
c: No, they do not meet at a right angle
No, they cross in the middle
Yes, they meet at a right angle
items.e: AB goes straight across and CD goes straight up. They cross at a right angle, so they are perpendicular.

items.q: Which pair of lines is perpendicular?
items.e: Picture B shows two lines that cross at a right angle. The other crossing lines meet at a slant.

items.q: What does the small square in the corner show?
c: The lines are the same length
The lines meet at a right angle
items.e: The small square is the sign for a right angle. So these lines are perpendicular.

items.q: Which pair of lines is perpendicular?
items.e: Picture C shows lines that do not touch, but if we make the short line longer, it meets the other line at a right angle. So they are perpendicular.

items.q: These two lines are perpendicular. How many right angles do they make where they cross?
items.e: Where two perpendicular lines cross, they make 4 square corners: 4 right angles.

items.q: Are lines AB and CD perpendicular?
c: No, they do not meet at a right angle
Yes, they would meet at a right angle
items.e: AB is vertical and CD is horizontal. If we make CD longer to the left, it meets AB at a right angle.

items.q: Are lines AB and CD perpendicular?
c: Yes, they would meet at a right angle
No, they do not meet at a right angle
items.e: If we make CD longer, it meets AB at a right angle. Perpendicular lines do not need to touch in the picture.

items.q: Devi says AB and CD are not parallel because CD is shorter. Is she right?
c: No, parallel lines can be different lengths
Yes, parallel lines must be the same length
items.e: Both lines go straight across and stay 2 squares apart. Length does not matter: they are parallel.

items.q: Are lines AB and CD parallel?
c: Yes, they stay the same distance apart
Yes, they are the same length
items.e: AB goes up to the right, but CD goes down to the right. They slant different ways, so they are not parallel.

items.q: What are parallel lines?
c: lines that are the same length
lines that stay the same distance apart and never meet
lines that cross in the middle
lines that meet at a right angle
items.e: Parallel lines always stay the same distance apart, like railway tracks. They never meet, however long they are.

items.q: Line AB is horizontal. Line CD is parallel to AB. What kind of line is CD?
items.e: A line parallel to a horizontal line goes the same way: straight across. So CD is horizontal.

items.q: Are lines AB and CD parallel?
c: Yes, they stay the same distance apart
No, they get closer and would meet
items.e: Both lines go 2 squares right and 4 squares up. They slant the same way, so they are parallel.

items.q: If we make two parallel lines longer and longer, what happens?
c: They cross at a right angle
items.e: Parallel lines stay the same distance apart all the way along, so they never meet.

items.q: Are lines AB and CD parallel?
c: Yes, they stay the same distance apart
No, they get closer and would meet
items.e: AB goes straight across and CD goes straight up. They cross at a right angle, so they are perpendicular, not parallel.

items.q: Which capital letter has NO parallel lines?
items.e: The 2 lines of V meet at the bottom, so they are not parallel. E, Z and H all have lines going the same way.

items.q: Which pair of lines is parallel?
items.e: Picture C shows lines that stay the same distance apart all the way along. The lines that get closer would meet if they were longer.

items.q: What do the small arrows on these lines show?
items.e: Matching arrow signs on two lines show that the lines are parallel.

items.q: Are lines AB and CD parallel?
c: No, they get closer and would meet
Yes, they slant the same way
Yes, they stay the same distance apart
items.e: AB goes 2 right and 4 down, but CD goes 2 right and only 3 down. The gap changes, so they are not parallel.

items.q: Are lines AB and CD parallel?
c: Yes, they stay the same distance apart
No, they get closer and would meet
No, they are not the same length
items.e: AB goes 6 right and 3 up. CD goes 2 right and 1 up: for every 2 squares right, both go 1 square up. They are parallel even though CD is shorter.

items.q: Which pair of lines is NOT parallel?
items.e: Picture A shows lines that get closer together, so they would meet if they were longer. The other three pairs stay the same distance apart.

items.q: Which pair of lines is parallel?
items.e: Picture B shows slanting lines that stay the same distance apart. Slanting lines can be parallel too.

items.q: Are lines AB and CD parallel?
c: Yes, they stay the same distance apart
No, they get closer and would meet
items.e: Both lines go straight up and stay 3 squares apart. Vertical lines can be parallel.

items.q: Which capital letter has a pair of parallel lines?
items.e: The 2 upright lines of H are parallel. L, T and V have no lines going the same way.

items.q: Which pair of lines is parallel?
items.e: Picture D shows two lines of different lengths that stay the same distance apart. Parallel lines do not need to be the same length.

items.q: Raju says AB and CD cannot be parallel because they are slanting. Is he right?
c: No, they slant the same way and stay the same distance apart
Yes, parallel lines must go straight across
items.e: Both lines go 1 square right for every 1 square up. Slanting lines can be parallel.

items.q: Are lines AB and CD parallel?
c: No, they get closer and would meet
Yes, they stay the same distance apart
items.e: Both lines go straight across and stay 3 squares apart. So they are parallel.

items.q: Are lines AB and CD parallel?
c: Yes, they stay the same distance apart
No, they get closer and would meet
items.e: The gap is 2 squares on the left but 3 squares on the right. The lines are not the same distance apart, so they are not parallel.

sets.title: Find pairs of lines in shapes and letters

items.q: How many pairs of perpendicular sides does this parallelogram have?
items.e: None of the corners is a right angle, so no two sides are perpendicular. It has 2 pairs of parallel sides, but 0 pairs of perpendicular sides.

items.q: Which side of rectangle ABCD is parallel to AB?
items.e: AB is the top side and CD is the bottom side. They stay the same distance apart, so CD is parallel to AB.

items.q: How many pairs of perpendicular lines are in the capital letter E?
items.e: The upright line meets each of the 3 lines going across at a right angle. That is 3 pairs.

items.q: How many sides of this figure are perpendicular to AB?
items.e: AF, BC and DE go straight up and down, so all 3 are perpendicular to AB. DE does not touch AB, but it is still perpendicular.

items.q: Which two sides are perpendicular to AD?
items.e: AD goes straight up. AB and CD go straight across and meet AD at right angles. BC is slanting.

items.q: How many sides of this figure are parallel to AB?
items.e: AB goes straight across. CD and EF also go straight across, so 2 sides are parallel to AB.

items.q: How many pairs of parallel sides does this turned square have?
items.e: Turning a square does not change its sides. Opposite sides still stay the same distance apart: 2 pairs.

items.q: Which side of parallelogram ABCD is parallel to AD?
items.e: AD and BC slant the same way and stay the same distance apart. Slanting sides can be parallel.

items.q: Which sides of rectangle ABCD are perpendicular to AB?
items.e: AD and BC meet AB at the corners A and B. Both corners are right angles, so AD and BC are perpendicular to AB.

items.q: How many pairs of perpendicular sides does this shape have?
items.e: AB and AD meet at a right angle, and AD and CD meet at a right angle. That is 2 pairs. BC meets the others at a slant.

items.q: How many pairs of parallel sides does a rectangle have?
items.e: AB is parallel to CD, and AD is parallel to BC. That is 2 pairs. (4 is the number of sides.)

items.q: Which shape has NO perpendicular sides?
items.e: Picture B is a parallelogram: none of its corners is a right angle. The other shapes all have right angles.

items.q: Which side of trapezium ABCD is parallel to AB?
items.e: AB at the bottom and CD at the top both go straight across and stay the same distance apart. So CD is parallel to AB.

items.q: Which two sides of triangle ABC are perpendicular?
items.e: Sides AB and BC meet at corner B, which is a right angle. So AB and BC are perpendicular.

items.q: How many pairs of parallel sides does this trapezium have?
items.e: Only AB and CD are parallel. AD and BC get closer at the top. A trapezium has exactly 1 pair of parallel sides.

items.q: How many pairs of parallel lines are in the capital letter H?
items.e: Only the 2 upright lines are parallel: 1 pair. The middle line is perpendicular to them.

items.q: Are sides AD and BC of this trapezium parallel?
c: Yes, they are the same length
No, they get closer at the top
items.e: AD and BC lean towards each other: the gap is wider at the bottom than at the top. So they are not parallel.

items.q: How many pairs of parallel sides does this hexagon have?
items.e: Each side is parallel to the side opposite it. 6 sides make 3 pairs.

items.q: How many pairs of perpendicular sides does a rectangle have?
items.e: Each of the 4 corners is a right angle, and each corner has a pair of perpendicular sides: AB and BC, BC and CD, CD and AD, AD and AB. That is 4 pairs.

items.q: Which shape has exactly 1 pair of parallel sides?
items.e: Picture C is a trapezium: only its top and bottom are parallel. The rectangle and the parallelogram have 2 pairs, and the triangle has none.

sets.title: Parallel and perpendicular lines on a square grid

items.q: Which line is parallel to PQ?
items.e: PQ goes 3 squares right and 1 square up. Line B goes 3 squares right and 1 square up. The steps are the same, so B is parallel. Swapping the steps (1 right and 3 up) gives a different line.

items.q: Farah draws a line from point R. She wants it to be parallel to PQ. Which point should she join R to?
items.e: PQ goes 4 squares straight across. From R to B goes 4 squares straight across. Both go straight across, so the lines are parallel.

items.q: Which line is perpendicular to PQ?
items.e: PQ goes 4 squares straight across. Line A goes 4 squares straight up. So they meet at a right angle if we make them longer: A is perpendicular to PQ.

items.q: Chloe draws a line from point R. She wants it to be perpendicular to PQ. Which point should she join R to?
items.e: PQ goes 4 squares right and 2 squares up. From R to A goes 2 squares right and 4 squares down. Swap the steps (4 and 2) and turn the slant: up becomes down. 4 right and 2 down is only the mirror slant.

items.q: How many of the lines A to D are parallel to PQ?
items.e: PQ goes 4 right and 2 up. A goes 2 right and 1 up, and B goes 4 right and 2 up: both are parallel. C and D slant differently.

items.q: Which line is parallel to PQ?
items.e: PQ goes 4 squares straight across. Line B goes 3 squares straight across. Both go straight across, so B is parallel to PQ. Being shorter does not matter.

items.q: Which line is parallel to PQ?
items.e: PQ goes 4 squares right and 2 squares up. Line A goes 2 squares right and 1 square up. For every 2 squares right, both go 1 square up, so A is parallel. A line going 2 right and 1 down slants the other way.

items.q: Hafiz draws a line from point R. He wants it to be perpendicular to PQ. Which point should he join R to?
items.e: PQ goes 4 squares straight up. From R to D goes 4 squares straight across. PQ is vertical and the new line is horizontal, so they meet at a right angle if we make them longer.

items.q: Which line is parallel to PQ?
items.e: PQ goes 3 squares right and 3 squares down. Line D goes 4 squares right and 4 squares down. For every 1 square right, both go 1 square down, so D is parallel. The line going up to the right is perpendicular.

items.q: Line PQ goes 3 squares right and 1 square up. A line perpendicular to PQ goes …
items.e: Swap the steps and turn the slant: 1 square right and 3 squares down. 1 right and 3 up only swaps the numbers, so it is not a right angle.

items.q: Which line is perpendicular to PQ?
items.e: PQ goes 4 squares right and 2 squares up. Line B goes 2 squares right and 4 squares down. Swap the steps (2 and 4) and turn the slant: B is perpendicular. 4 right and 2 down is only the mirror slant, not a right angle.

items.q: Which line is parallel to PQ?
items.e: PQ goes 2 squares right and 4 squares down. Line D goes 2 squares right and 4 squares down. Both go the same steps, so D is parallel to PQ. Check the steps: 2 right and 3 down is a different slant.

items.q: Which line is perpendicular to PQ?
items.e: PQ goes 2 squares right and 4 squares down. Line A goes 4 squares right and 2 squares up. The steps 2 and 4 are swapped and the slant is turned, so A is perpendicular to PQ.

items.q: Which line is parallel to PQ?
items.e: PQ goes 6 squares straight up. Line C goes 4 squares straight up. Both go straight up, so C is parallel to PQ.

items.q: Which line is perpendicular to PQ?
items.e: PQ goes 6 squares straight up. Line C goes 4 squares straight across. So C is perpendicular to PQ, even though they do not touch.

items.q: Which line is perpendicular to PQ?
items.e: PQ goes 3 squares right and 3 squares down. Line C goes 3 squares right and 3 squares up. PQ goes down to the right and C goes up to the right, 1 square for every 1 square. They meet at a right angle.

items.q: Sarah draws a line from point R. She wants it to be parallel to PQ. Which point should she join R to?
items.e: PQ goes 3 squares right and 2 squares up. From R to C goes 6 squares right and 4 squares up. For every 3 squares right, both lines go 2 squares up, so they are parallel. Be careful: 2 right and 3 up swaps the steps.

items.q: Which line is perpendicular to PQ?
items.e: PQ goes 1 square right and 3 squares up. Line D goes 3 squares right and 1 square down. The steps 1 and 3 are swapped and the slant is turned, so D meets PQ at a right angle.

items.q: Line PQ goes 3 squares right and 1 square up. A line parallel to PQ goes …
items.e: A parallel line has the same steps: 3 squares right and 1 square up (it can start anywhere).

items.q: How many of the lines A to D are perpendicular to PQ?
items.e: PQ is vertical. Lines A, C and D go straight across, so all 3 are perpendicular to PQ. B is vertical: it is parallel to PQ.

sets.title: Parallel and perpendicular lines around us

items.q: Which road is parallel to School Road?
items.e: Park Road goes across the map, the same way as School Road, and they stay the same distance apart. So they are parallel.

items.q: How are the top and bottom edges of this window frame?
items.e: The top and bottom edges both go straight across and stay the same distance apart. They are parallel.

items.q: How are the rungs (steps) of this ladder to each other?
items.e: All the rungs go straight across and stay the same distance apart, so they are parallel.

items.q: Ethan draws a ladder on square grid paper. The first rung goes 4 squares straight across. How should he draw the next rung?
items.e: The rungs must be parallel, so the next rung goes the same way: straight across.

items.q: At which of these times are the hands of a clock perpendicular?
items.e: At 9 o’clock the hands point to 12 and 9: 3 hour marks apart, a right angle. At 6 o’clock they make a straight line.

items.q: On Sports Day, Wei Ming runs in lane 3 on the straight part of the track. How are the lines of his lane?
c: they meet at the finish line
items.e: The two lines of a lane stay the same distance apart, so every runner has the same room. They are parallel.

items.q: Ali looks along a long MRT track. The rails look as if they meet far away. Are the rails parallel?
c: Yes, they only look closer far away
No, they really meet far away
items.e: Things far away look smaller, so the gap looks smaller. The real gap stays the same, so the rails are parallel.

items.q: Look at the hands of the clock. Are they perpendicular?
c: No, they make a straight line
Yes, they make a right angle
No, the angle is too small
items.e: At 3 o’clock the minute hand points to 12 and the hour hand points to 3. They make a right angle, so they are perpendicular.

items.q: Jun Jie folds a square piece of paper in half, then in half again the other way. He opens it. How are the two fold lines?
items.e: The second fold goes across the first fold at a right angle, so the fold lines are perpendicular.

items.q: The two bars of this window cross in the middle. How are the bars?
items.e: One bar is vertical and one is horizontal. They cross at a right angle, so they are perpendicular.

items.q: The brown bars under the rails are called sleepers. How is each sleeper to the rails?
items.e: Each sleeper goes across the rails at a right angle, so it is perpendicular to the rails.

items.q: Which road is perpendicular to School Road?
items.e: Lake Avenue goes straight up and down the map and meets School Road at a right angle.

items.q: Hui Min says Market Street is perpendicular to School Road because they cross. Is she right?
c: Yes, it goes up and down
Yes, roads that cross are perpendicular
No, Market Street crosses at a slant
items.e: Market Street slants. It crosses School Road, but not at a right angle, so it is not perpendicular.

items.q: Look at the hands of the clock. Are they perpendicular?
c: Yes, they meet in the middle
No, the angle is smaller than a right angle
No, they make a straight line
Yes, they make a right angle
items.e: At 1 o’clock the hands are only 1 hour mark apart. A right angle needs 3 hour marks, so they are not perpendicular.

items.q: How are the two rails of a railway track?
items.e: The rails stay the same distance apart all the way, so the train wheels can run on them. They are parallel.

items.q: Kavya folds a long strip of paper in half, then in half again the same way. She opens it. How are the fold lines?
items.e: Every fold goes the same way across the strip, so the fold lines are parallel.

items.q: Which of these is NOT a pair of parallel lines?
c: the two rails of a railway track
the two lines of a running lane
the hands of a clock at 3 o’clock
the top and bottom edges of a door
items.e: The hands at 3 o’clock meet at a right angle: they are perpendicular. The others stay the same distance apart.

items.q: In an HDB flat, the floor is horizontal and a wall is vertical. How are the floor and the wall?
items.e: A horizontal floor meets a vertical wall at a right angle, so they are perpendicular.

items.q: How is each rung of the ladder to the two side rails?
items.e: Each rung meets the side rails at a right angle, so the rungs are perpendicular to the side rails.

items.q: How are the white stripes of this zebra crossing?
items.e: Every stripe goes the same way and the stripes stay the same distance apart. They are parallel.
